The Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has called on Nigerians to embrace peace, unity and mutual understanding in addressing the challenges confronting the country. The Sultan made the call on Wednesday when he received the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress and former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, alongside members of his delegation, during a courtesy visit to his palace in Sokoto. He stressed the importance of collective responsibility in nation-building, noting that traditional institutions had critical roles to play in promoting peaceful coexistence, national unity and sustainable development. The Sultan said, “Peace, unity and mutual understanding are essential for addressing the challenges facing our nation. We must all embrace collective responsibility towards building a better society.” He also emphasised the need for Nigerians to work together irrespective of their political, religious and ethnic differences. Atiku said, “We appreciate His Eminence for the warm reception accorded to us. Traditional rulers have an important role to play in promoting peace, unity and national development.” He reaffirmed the need for collective efforts towards building a better and more prosperous Nigeria. The visit provided an opportunity for discussions on issues of national importance and the continued promotion of peace, unity and development. The Sultan was accompanied during the visit by the Wazirin Sokoto, Magajin Rafin Sokoto, Galadiman Garin Sokoto, Sa’in Kilgori and the Secretary of the Sultanate Council. Animashaun Salman
